page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the DLDSv5 family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The server features 48 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes a local 1843 GB SSD for storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the D48lds_v5 in the average performance tier for most standard operations, with notable strengths in specific multi-threaded and cryptographic tasks. The server achieved a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 218.81 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU encryption score of 41,963.43, both ranking in the strong category. Geekbench image processing also performed strongly at 15,483.0. In contrast, LLM inference on a large 70B model for text generation was weak at 2.75 tokens/sec, though smaller 135M model text generation reached a strong 269.44 tokens/sec. Standard CPU benchmarks, such as the PassMark CPU score of 47,311.76 and Geekbench multi-core score of 15,804.0, fall within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the D48lds_v5 offers a high concentration of compute cores relative to its memory capacity. This low-memory design provides a cost-efficient option for workloads that require substantial parallel processing power without the overhead of large memory footprints. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a significant tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, which may experience bottlenecks. The inclusion of a 1843 GB local SSD adds value for tasks requiring fast local scratch space, avoiding the need for external storage attachments for temporary data.

This server configuration is suitable for compute-heavy workloads that do not demand extensive memory allocations. Appropriate use cases include multi-threaded data decompression, cryptographic processing, image processing, software compilation, and web serving. It is also viable for small-scale language model inference, though it is not suited for large-scale model generation or memory-bound database systems.
